transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling extremely down and sad for the past five months. It feels like this heavy, depressed mood just won't lift, and I'm constantly exhausted. I just really felt like I needed to get some help.
Have you ever had periods lasting at least a few days where you felt the opposite of down—like you had unusually high energy, needed very little sleep, or felt extremely wired and active?

Yes, I actually had a period like that for about four months where I felt an incredible overflow of physical and mental energy. I was extremely active and found it absolutely impossible to sit still or rest. It felt like I was constantly driven to keep moving.
During that high-energy period, did it cause major problems in your work or relationships, or did you ever need to be hospitalized because of it?
No, I've never been hospitalized for it. I'm also not quite sure if it caused any major problems in my work or relationships back then.
During either your high-energy periods or your down periods, did you ever hear or see things that others couldn't, or hold strong beliefs that others told you weren't real?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never heard or seen things that weren't really there, and I haven't held any beliefs that others found unusual.
During that four-month period of high energy, did friends or family comment on how different or unusually active you seemed?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't recall if my friends or family ever commented on how I was acting during those months.
During that four-month period of high energy, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual—like feeling fully rested after only a few hours?
I don't recall having a reduced need for sleep during that time. I didn't really notice that being the case, so I think my sleep was pretty normal.
During that four-month period of high energy, did you feel like your thoughts were racing or that you were talking much faster than usual?
I don't recall my thoughts racing or talking faster than usual during that time. I really don't think that was happening.
During that four-month period of high energy, did you find yourself making impulsive decisions or taking risks that you wouldn't normally take, like spending too much money?
I don't recall making any particularly impulsive decisions or taking unusual risks during that period. I also don't think I spent excessively or did anything out of the ordinary in that regard.
During that four-month period of high energy, did you feel much more confident than usual, or feel like you had special talents or powers that others didn't?
No, I didn't feel like I had any special talents or powers. While I definitely had a lot of energy back then, my confidence felt pretty normal and I didn't think I was superior to anyone else.
During these past five months of feeling down, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing?

Yes, absolutely. For the past five months, I've completely lost interest in all of my usual hobbies and activities. I just don't feel any pleasure or joy from doing them anymore, and everything feels completely empty.

Therefore, Major Depressive Disorder is highly likely, but Bipolar I and II Disorders remain in the differential until we can fully rule out hypomanic/manic episodes. Persistent Depressive Disorder is also considered.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a five-month episode of severe depressive symptoms, including a persistent depressed mood, constant exhaustion, and a complete loss of interest and pleasure (anhedonia) in normal activities, which aligns with Major Depressive Disorder. Although the patient described a prior four-month period of high energy, this episode did not meet the diagnostic criteria for mania or hypomania because they denied key accompanying symptoms such as decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, grandiosity, or impulsive behaviors, thereby ruling out Bipolar I and Bipolar II disorders.
